name: ImageSpace
tagline: A local-first layered image studio in C#, on desktop and the web
summary: ImageSpace is an independent layered image editor built with Uno Platform, SkiaSharp and an optional WebGPU compute backend. Its photo-editing workspace runs as a genuine Uno WebAssembly application and shares its C# editor with Windows, Linux and macOS hosts. Eleven reusable .NET libraries separate the tile-based document model, brushes, selections, filters, transactions, file formats, rendering, controls, viewport and workbench.

highlights.title: Genuine Uno WebAssembly
highlights.text: The browser workspace is a real Uno app sharing its C# editor with desktop hosts — not a monolithic canvas or an HTML mockup.

highlights.title: Layers, type and shapes
highlights.text: Sparse pixel layers, editable multiline type and rectangle/ellipse shapes with sixteen blend modes, opacity, locks and reordering.

highlights.title: Pressure-aware painting
highlights.text: Brush, pencil, eraser and clone with size, hardness, opacity and flow, plus basic smudge, dodge and burn.

highlights.title: Non-destructive Curves & Levels
highlights.text: Adjustment layers with composite RGB and per-channel graphs, numeric and keyboard editing, presets and live undoable previews.

highlights.title: Independent masks
highlights.text: Pixel, type, shape and adjustment masks with density, feather, unlinked affine placement and a separate Apply layer mask workflow.

highlights.title: Rich selections
highlights.text: Rectangle, ellipse, lasso and contiguous color with add/subtract/intersect, feather, expand, contract, border and smooth.

highlights.title: Optional WebGPU compute
highlights.text: A reusable browser WebGPU module accelerates eight color kernels, with an explicit CPU fallback and the tile model as source of truth.

highlights.title: Copy-on-write tiles
highlights.text: Sparse 128-pixel RGBA tiles with copy-on-write snapshots power transactional undo without copying every pixel per stroke.

items: Pressure-aware brush, pencil and eraser with size, hardness, opacity and flow
Clone from an Alt-click source on the active layer
Basic smudge, dodge and burn
Fill and linear gradient on the active pixel layer
Color spectrum, hex dialog and foreground/background swatches
Rectangle, ellipse, lasso and contiguous color selection
Add, subtract and intersect with Shift, Alt and Shift+Alt
Invert, feather and alpha selection
Expand, contract, border and smooth that preserve soft coverage
Pixel, editable multiline type and rectangle/ellipse shape layers
Sixteen blend modes, opacity, visibility, locks, duplicate, reorder and rasterize
Masks on pixel, type, shape and adjustment layers with density and feather
Unlink masks to move, rotate and resize coverage; relink without a jump
Grayscale and red-overlay mask inspection views
Apply layer mask bakes coverage into pixel alpha as one undoable edit
Curves with 2–16 points per channel and shape-preserving cubic interpolation
Levels with input black/white, gamma and output endpoints
Live adjustments: brightness/contrast, saturation, invert, grayscale, sepia, blur
Fourteen CPU color/convolution filters that respect selections
Eight optional WebGPU kernels with CPU fallback
Eight-handle scaling, rotation and constrained motion
Numeric X/Y/W/H/Angle properties
Non-destructive crop with thirds guides that preserves off-canvas pixels
Canvas size and image size; wheel zoom, Space to pan, rulers and pixel grid
Editable .imagespace archives (reader accepts versions 1–4)
Bounded PSD v1 RGB/8 import and export, including placed user masks
PNG, JPEG and WebP import and composite export
Up to twelve document tabs
Local IndexedDB or atomic desktop recovery of the active document

codeSamples.title: Embed the viewport
Build and run
codeSamples.code:
dotnet workload install wasm-tools --skip-manifest-update
python3 scripts/fetch-assets.py

# Native desktop host.
dotnet run --project src/ImageSpace.App -f net10.0-desktop -p:ImageSpaceDesktopOnly=true

# Genuine Uno browser application, with the GitHub Pages project prefix.
dotnet publish src/ImageSpace.App -c Release -f net10.0-browserwasm \
  -p:WasmShellWebAppBasePath=/ImageSpace/ -o artifacts/publish
python3 scripts/collect-site.py artifacts/publish site
python3 scripts/serve-site.py --root site --port 4173

playground.intro: Open the live WebAssembly workspace and edit the original After the light sample — pixel, type and shape layers are ready to explore.

tour.title: Explore the layers
tour.text: Select the sky, dune, type and shape layers in the Layers panel, or press V and click visible content to pick and transform it.

tour.title: Paint on a new layer
tour.text: Add a pixel layer with +, press B for the brush, change size with [ and ], and tune hardness, opacity and flow.

tour.title: Add a Curves layer
tour.text: Choose Image → Curves adjustment layer, click to add points and drag them; the preview updates live and Escape cancels.

tour.title: Mask the adjustment
tour.text: Make a selection with M or L, add a layer mask, then paint black to hide and white to reveal; try the red Overlay view.

tour.title: Apply a filter
tour.text: Run a filter on a selection; supported browser kernels use WebGPU when available, otherwise the CPU path.

tour.title: Save and export
tour.text: Press Ctrl+S to download an editable .imagespace archive, or export the composite as PNG, JPEG or WebP.

architecture.name: Core model
architecture.text: Straight-alpha RGBA8 pixels in sparse 128×128 copy-on-write tiles, layers and tone math.

architecture.name: Raster engines and files
architecture.text: Brushes, selections and filters operate on the tile model; native archives and PSD are read and written here.

architecture.name: Transactions and rendering
architecture.text: Transactional history over tiles, a revision-cached Skia compositor and an optional parallel WebGPU compute service.

architecture.name: Uno controls and viewport
architecture.text: Custom controls and an embeddable viewport drawing into Uno's SKCanvasElement.

architecture.name: Workbench
architecture.text: Panels, menus and multi-document workflows, with hosts injecting file and recovery storage.

boundaries: Follows familiar Photoshop conventions but is not pixel-identical or at full Photoshop parity
PSD is bounded RGB/8 raster interchange: no smart objects, groups, clipping chains or ICC profiles
No layer groups, pen/path editor, layer styles, healing/content-aware tools or Camera Raw
Working limits: 8192 px per side, 16 megapixels per surface, 128 layers and twelve documents
WebGPU accelerates eight color kernels only; it is not a GPU-only engine
